key_insight: An open-source process finite-element pipeline combined with SSO-tuned surrogates can reliably guide IGBT module reliability design, but optimizer decisions must be rechecked with new FEA because surrogate error can grow at the design-space edges.
engineering_relevance: For power-module packaging, the study shows how surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization can accelerate warpage and stress trade studies while preserving design credibility through confirmation FEA and infill updates.
method: Open-source process FEA model of IGBT/DBC module warpage and reliability metrics
Train and tune surrogate regressors with Simplified Swarm Optimization
Run multi-objective search, then confirm selected Pareto designs with new FEA and infill retraining
evidence_signal: The model matched measured warpage within 18.2%, 33.6%, and 15.3% across processing stages; confirmed designs showed warpage MAE of 0.5%, while ceramic-stress error reached up to 26% before infill reduced it to 1-10%.
watch_item: Ceramic-stress predictions are mesh-sensitive and can be overly optimistic at optimizer-explored boundaries, so design decisions should not rely on surrogate outputs alone.
paper_title: Simplified Swarm Optimization for Surrogate-Assisted Reliability Design of Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistor Power Modules Using an Open-Source Process Finite-Element Model
